artifacts.summary: Seven-phase, 10-hour lean4 plan for the nomic operator, thm:nomic-uniform, prop:nomic-tense-free, seriality and app:nomic-four, with 40 pinned Challenge statements.

memory_candidates.content: A semantics whose evaluation point is not (TaskModel F, WorldHistory F, F.Duration) over a TaskFrame cannot instantiate FormalSystem/Semantics/TruthClauses.lean at all: every clause class there (BotClause, ImpClause, BoxClause, UntlClause, SnceClause, StabClause) repeats that exact binder set. The concrete blocker for a nomic semantics is that H_F is a union of per-state law-history sets and, on a non-uniform frame, is the world-history set of no single task frame, so the WorldHistory F binder cannot be met. The consequence is a re-derived derived-operator clause layer -- nine short lemmas (neg, and, iff, someFuture, allFuture, somePast, allPast, always, next), each 3-8 lines, with only the two collapsed forms (always to the forall-y normal form via lt_trichotomy, and next via Order.succ) carrying content. Generalising the clause layer over the point structure is a six-component refactor across every language directory and is not worth it for one consumer; record the duplication and its cause in the new truth module's docstring instead. The same verdict will apply to any future neighbourhood or two-dimensional semantics in this tree.
